cases.description: A challenge signed by the RP's active key, verified at a clock inside its window, verifies and derives its grantId.
A challenge verified at exactly issuedAt is inside the window (inclusive lower bound).
A bare-host did:web rp carrying a non-default port derives an origin with that port, and a redirectUri under it verifies.
An active key whose validFrom/validUntil bracket the verifier clock verifies the challenge.
A retired RP key MUST NOT verify a live challenge, so the signature step rejects even though the key material matches.
A revoked RP key never verifies a challenge.
An active key whose validUntil precedes the verifier clock is out of window and does not verify; usability is evaluated at now, not at the RP-chosen issuedAt.
An active key whose validFrom is after the verifier clock is not yet usable and does not verify.
A candidate active key that is not the signing key cannot verify the signature.
An empty candidate key set yields no usable active signing key, so the signature step rejects.
Changing redirectUri after signing to another value under the same origin keeps the schema valid but breaks the signature.
Changing the nonce after signing breaks the signature.
An unknown top-level field is rejected by the strict schema before verification.
The challenge type is a single new spelling; the grant type is not accepted.
There is no legacy network.tulpa spelling of the challenge type; only network.ink.authorization_challenge is accepted.
A protocol other than ink/0.1 is out of profile and rejects.
A lone UTF-16 surrogate in a string field is not portable and rejects as schema before the signature.
A path-bearing did:web has no unambiguous origin and rejects as schema before the signature.
An uppercase host label is not a bytewise-comparable A-label and rejects.
A final label that is all digits is excluded, matching the hostname rule that a top-level label is never all-numeric.
A dotted-quad IPv4 literal fails the label grammar (its final label is all-numeric) and rejects.
An explicit port 443 is out of profile because its derived origin would collide with the default.
The port marker MUST be an uppercase %3A; a lowercase %3a leaves a percent in the host and rejects.
A requestedScope that does not include identity.assert is not a sign-in request and rejects.
A requestedScope entry outside the registry is malformed on the request side and rejects.
A repeated requestedScope entry is rejected; entries must be distinct so two implementations count the same set.
A requestedScope with no entries is out of profile and rejects.
A requestedScope with a non-string entry rejects.
A redirectUri that is not the derived RP origin plus / rejects under the literal prefix rule.
A redirectUri whose host merely extends the RP host is not the origin plus /, because the / defeats suffix extension, and rejects.
A redirectUri equal to the origin with no trailing / rejects; the prefix is the origin followed immediately by /.
A redirectUri containing # is malformed: a fragment never reaches the completion endpoint.
A redirectUri containing a backslash is rejected; parsers disagree on backslash normalization.
A redirectUri containing an ASCII control character is rejected; a control char that survives into a Location header is an injection primitive.
A redirectUri containing ASCII whitespace is rejected; the string is not trimmed first.
A nonce shorter than 16 code units is out of profile and rejects.
A challenge whose expiresAt is not after issuedAt is malformed and rejects.
A window exceeding the ten-minute maximum lifetime is out of profile and rejects structurally, before the signature, even against a wrong key.
A signature that is not valid base64url of the right length is rejected.
A challenge with no signature field rejects.
A challenge whose issuedAt is not a strict INK timestamp rejects.
A challenge verified after expiresAt is rejected.
A challenge verified at exactly expiresAt is rejected (exclusive upper bound).
A challenge verified before issuedAt is rejected.
A verifier clock that is not a strict INK timestamp is a verifier input error and fails closed as schema, not a window verdict.
A challenge with a tampered body verified after expiry rejects on the signature, not on expiry, pinning signature-before-window order.
A challenge with a tampered body verified before issuedAt rejects on the signature, not on the window.
An active signing key whose validUntil equals the verifier clock is still usable (inclusive upper bound), so the challenge verifies.
An active signing key whose validFrom equals the verifier clock is usable (inclusive lower bound), so the challenge verifies.
A trailing dot leaves an empty final label, which fails the label grammar, so the rp rejects.
A second %3A in the port position is a malformed identifier and rejects.
Port 0 is out of the 1..65535 range and rejects.
Port 65536 is one past the maximum and rejects.
A bracketed IPv6 literal fails the label grammar (brackets and colons are not LDH), so it rejects without a separate exclusion.
A percent escape in the host (a percent-encoded dot) is malformed: the host carries no percent-encoding, so it rejects.
The literal-prefix match is case-sensitive: an uppercase host in the redirectUri does not equal the derived lowercase origin and rejects.
A trailing dot on the redirectUri host breaks the literal prefix (the character after the origin is a dot, not /) and rejects.
A redirectUri that is the origin plus / plus a query only (no path segment) satisfies the prefix rule and verifies.
The same signed challenge presented as raw wire text verifies: whitespace between tokens is legal JSON and vanishes at canonicalization, so the signature still covers it.

An out-of-range number literal shadowed by a later duplicate member rejects. Member semantics are last-wins, so the literal never reaches the parsed challenge and the signature over the canonical form still verifies; only a gate on the raw text sees it, and without one two implementations admit different byte strings for the same signed challenge.
An out-of-range number literal in a live member rejects at the raw gate, before the schema can rule on the Infinity a lenient parser would hand it.
An underflowing exponent is in range: every IEEE-754 parser decodes 1e-400 to 0, so a shadowed one is not gated and the challenge behind it verifies. The gate is a range test, not a ban on exponents.
A lone UTF-16 surrogate escape in the raw text rejects structurally, before the signature: a parser that rewrites it to U+FFFD would canonicalize something other than what was sent.
The derived grantId over the four binding fields is deterministic and matches the pinned base64url-nopad SHA-256 digest.
A challenge sharing the four binding fields but differing in requestedScope and redirectUri derives the identical id, so the binding is over exactly rp, nonce, issuedAt, and expiresAt.
A challenge differing only in rp derives a distinct id, so the same nonce at two RPs cannot collide.
A challenge differing only in nonce derives a distinct id.
A challenge differing only in its window derives a distinct id, so a reused nonce in a fresh window cannot collide.
